# Pilot

> Pilot is a local bridge so any agent harness can drive a Chrome profile:
> clicks, keys, typing, form fills, tab management, and small screenshots. It
> does not steal your window. It is free and open source under the MIT licence.

## What it is

Pilot has three pieces:

- A Chrome extension (Manifest V3). It connects to the relay when the browser
  starts. The popup shows the state and can disconnect.
- A relay, `server.js`. It runs on localhost. One relay serves every Chrome
  profile on the machine.
- A command-line client, `cli.js`. The harness sends it JSON actions, for
  example `node cli.js '{"action":"snap"}'`.

It also includes `ocr.swift`, an on-device OCR tool that uses macOS Vision. It
reads screenshot text with no API key.

## How an agent drives a page

- `snap` returns the page text and a numbered list of clickable items.
- `clickN` clicks an item by its number. The agent then snaps again to check.
- Clicks and keys go through the Chrome debugger, so pages get real, trusted
  input. If the tab is in the window you are using, Pilot sends simulated
  events instead, so your focus is not touched.
- Each agent uses `--session NAME` and gets its own pinned tab. Two agents do
  not drive the same tab.
- `--profile NAME` picks which connected Chrome profile to drive.
- Commands to a profile that is not connected wait on the relay until it
  connects.

## Install

1. Clone https://github.com/FatherMarz/pilot
2. Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
3. Click Load unpacked and select the `extension/` folder.
4. Run the relay with `node server.js`. A harness normally starts it for you.

## Cost and licence

Free. MIT licence.
